name: Undercity
summary: Beneath the shattered ruins of Lordaeron's capital lies the Undercity, the dark stronghold of the Forsaken. Lady Sylvanas Windrunner took it from the Scourge, and made it a sanctuary no enemy can breach. Today it is the seat of Forsaken power. And it is the Horde's great bastion, in the north of the Eastern Kingdoms.

sections.title: From Royal Crypts to Scourge Redoubt
sections.body:
Long before the plague, the catacombs and sewers beneath the palace were already called the Undercity. Nobles lay entombed there, beside the poorest people of the realm. And there lay the kingdom's deepest prisons. Even Orgrim Doomhammer, the former Warchief, was held in them before he escaped.

In the Third War, Arthas Menethil murdered King Terenas, and laid waste to the capital. Then the prince set his undead servants to dig. They widened the old passages into a fortified seat of Scourge rule. But the Scourge never saw their dark capital finished.

sections.title: Rise of the Forsaken
sections.body: When the Lich King's power waned, Lady Sylvanas Windrunner broke free of his will, and took thousands of undead with her. She ambushed Arthas, and he fled back to Northrend. A vicious civil war followed, against the Scourge remnants, the dreadlords and the human resistance. Out of it, Sylvanas claimed the half-finished catacombs. She named her people the Forsaken, and oversaw years of labor on the sprawling city.

sections.title: Architecture of the Damned
sections.body: The city spreads in rings around the Trade Quarter, and great lifts join it to the palace ruins above. Around it lie the other quarters, and among them is the toxic Apothecarium. There the Royal Apothecary Society brews virulent plagues, beside canals of green slime. Deeper still, the Banshee Queen holds court in the Royal Quarter, with her dreadlord commander Varimathras. Legions of towering abominations stand guard.

faq.q: What was the Undercity before the undead took it over?
faq.answer: Beneath the palace of Lordaeron lay the ancient crypts of human royalty, along with the city's dungeon complex and vast sewer network. It housed prisoners of war, including Orgrim Doomhammer, as well as destitute citizens living in the subterranean shadows. The dungeons beneath the palace were already called the Undercity. After sacking the capital, Prince Arthas began turning these catacombs into a Scourge fortress before Sylvanas captured them.

faq.q: Why is the city built underground instead of on the surface?
faq.answer: The surface city of Lordaeron was utterly ruined during the Third War, making it difficult to defend against the Scarlet Crusade, Scourge forces, and Alliance survivors. The subterranean tunnels offered natural fortification, choke points, and secrecy, allowing the Forsaken to complete the Scourge's initial construction and thrive unseen.

The city is ruled by Lady Sylvanas Windrunner, the Banshee Queen and Queen of the Forsaken. She governs from the Royal Quarter, guarded by Forsaken royal sentries and her subjugated dreadlord lieutenant, Varimathras. Sylvanas broke free of the Lich King's will after the battle of Mount Hyjal. The city also has a War Quarter, Rogues' Quarter, and Magic Quarter.

faq.q: What is King Terenas's memorial in the ruins above?
aliases: who built the tomb above undercity
faq.answer: Above the city's main lifts sits a stone memorial for the slain King Terenas Menethil II. It does not contain his body, as his corpse was cremated and his ashes discarded during Kel'Thuzad's resurrection. Surviving Alliance humans bravely carved the monument amidst the ruins so the memory of Lordaeron's last true king would endure.

faq.q: What are the strange noises in the Lordaeron throne room?
faq.answer: In the ruined throne room above the Undercity lifts, spectral echoes of the past still linger. Visitors standing in the center can hear faint phantom sounds: the celebratory bells and rose petals of Arthas's return, the warning words of the prophet Medivh, and the final conversation between King Terenas and his patricidal son.

faq.q: Why do the Forsaken allow other Horde members here?
aliases: why is undercity part of horde
faq.answer: The Forsaken formed an alliance of convenience with Warchief Thrall's Horde for survival, surrounded as they are by hostile Scarlet zealots and Scourge legions. While living Horde races find the toxic fumes and alchemical rivers stifling, emissaries and travelers are allowed access to foster diplomatic and military ties.

angles.text: The Undercity is your sovereign sanctuary and homeland, carved out by your own hands after breaking the Lich King's iron grip on your mind.
As the Horde's primary foothold in the Eastern Kingdoms, the Undercity secures zeppelin links directly back to Durotar and Grom'gol Base Camp.
Beneath the soil of your fallen ancestral kingdom lies a grim perversion of Lordaeron's royal crypts, occupied by the walking corpses of your former brethren.
Deep within these very dungeons, the legendary Warchief Orgrim Doomhammer was once imprisoned by the Alliance of Lordaeron before making his historic escape.
